newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett off after work station price cuts.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett off after work station price cuts.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co shares on Tuesday extended the losses that began late yesterday after the company announced cuts in its workstation prices.
In early New York Stock Exchange trade, the shares were off 1-1/8 to 52-1/8. Earlier, they had been as low as 51-1/2.

The decline began Monday when, with one hour remaining in the trading day, the company said it would cut prices by up to 41 percent as part of a new plan designed give it a lead in workstation price-performance.
In the final hour of trading Monday, Hewlett shares fell one point to close at 53-1/4.
Analysts said the new pricing was aimed at countering recent market share gains by Sun Microsystems Inc.

Last week International Data Corp reported that Sun Micro had raised its market share in the UNIX workstation business in 1996 to 41 percent from 38.1 percent. Its share was larger than that of its closest three rivals combined, IDC said.
Hewlett remained in second place, but its share fell slightly to 19 percent of units shipped, according to IDC.
Market share on a revenues basis also had Sun Micro first and Hewlett second, with Sun taking 32 percent and Hewlett 21.4 percent.
Sun Micro shares were unchanged in morning Nasdaq trade at 32-1/4.
